transcript:
HEADER
Date: 2025-04-09
Start: 2025-04-09T16:00:00Z
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Evan Chen (Head of ML, Lighthouse); Maya Torres (Platform Eng); Sanjay Patel (SRE)

SUMMARY:
Customer is evaluating a migration off OpenAI hosted endpoints to Redwood Dedicated to reduce unit cost and gain more control over data residency and keys. Primary concerns: eval parity with current OpenAI outputs, performance parity (latency/p95), operational work for vLLM/TGI parity, VPC/on-prem options, and enterprise security (SOC 2, KMS, audit logs).

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on this — quick intros?
[00:07] Evan Chen: Evan here, head of ML at Lighthouse, we're running chat product + embeddings currently on OpenAI.
[00:12] Maya Torres: Maya, platform engineer, I'll own infra side and networking.
[00:16] Sanjay Patel: Sanjay, SRE, I'll look at ops and runbooks.
[00:20] Priya Nair: Priya, solutions engineer, i'll focus on perf and benchmarks.

[02:05] Jordan Lee: High level, why are you looking to move? cost was mentioned in the form, any specifics — per token cost or latency issues?
[02:14] Evan Chen: Yeah both really. We're hitting growth where OpenAI per-token costs are getting expensive. Also need more control for data residency and key mgmt for compliance, and we want lower tail latency for chat.
[02:28] Maya Torres: And we need VPC connectivity to our private infra; can't route certain data through public endpoints.

[05:12] Priya Nair: Got it. Quick note on compatibility: we often see customers worry about prompt/response parity. If you're using GPT-4 style prompts, we can run parity evals against your prompt set — run both on your current OpenAI calls and on Redwood Dedicated with the same model family, quantization, and runtime (we support vLLM/TGI backends), then measure qual/metric diffs.
[05:36] Evan Chen: That part's key — we have 1200 prompt pairs we use for regression testing, plus a few system messages that are pretty sensitive.

[08:00] Jordan Lee: Perfect, we'll ask you to share a sample subset. On the infra side — Redwood Dedicated offers dedicated GPU pools with VPC peering and private network options, plus customer-managed KMS/HSM for keys.
[08:18] Maya Torres: For KMS, we use GCP KMS in project X, but we can consider HSM. How does Redwood handle key rotation and encryption-at-rest?
[08:29] Priya Nair: We integrate with cloud KMS providers and can do bring-your-own-key (BYOK) flows. Rotation is supported and logs are exported to the audit bucket. We'll share the SOC2 and network diagram docs.

[12:10] Sanjay Patel: On the runtime — we're running vLLM internally and also evaluating TGI for some opt workloads; are there any behavioral differences we should expect when moving to Redwood-managed runtime?
[12:23] Priya Nair: Good question. Redwood's serving runtime is GPU-optimized; for the most part model outputs match when using the same model weights and tokenizer. Differences can come from decoding seeds, temperature handling, and beam/stop token handling. We'll do parity tests and also provide config knobs: random seeds, logits processors, and temperature controls so we can align outputs.
[12:45] Evan Chen: Are you shipping the same open-model weights or do you host your own forks? We currently call OpenAI hosted endpoints for GPT-like models.
[12:55] Jordan Lee: We host curated open weights from model registries and also can support customer-provided weights. For customers that need exact parity with OpenAI's closed models there's often a small delta; we recommend an eval to quantify. If you need identical outputs for regulatory reasons, we can discuss hybrid routing (fallback to hosted).

[16:01] Maya Torres: Throughput and batching are important — our product does a lot of short-turn chat with many concurrent users. How does Redwood handle batching without increasing latency?
[16:12] Priya Nair: Redwood uses continuous batching with latency SLOs. You can configure per-route latency targets; the runtime will favor lower-latency scheduling for chat routes and more aggressive batching for background embedding jobs. We also have KV/prefix caching to reduce repeated context costs.

[19:45] Evan Chen: What about autoscaling and predictable throughput for Dedicated? We need predictable p95 latency at peak times.
[19:53] Jordan Lee: Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools and configurable autoscaling policies — you can set min/max nodes and burst capacity. We also have canary deploys and automatic fallback policies if a model variant is unavailable.

[23:30] Sanjay Patel: Security: SOC2 and audit logs, SSO, RBAC — how mature is that? We need logs for 12 months and integration with our SIEM.
[23:40] Priya Nair: We support SSO/SAML, fine-grained RBAC, and exportable audit logs. Retention is configurable as an add-on; we'll share the SOC2 report and audit log export docs.

[27:10] Evan Chen: On the benchmarking — we'd like to test both output quality (F1/ROUGE-ish metrics, plus manual eval) and latency/cost. Is there an example benchmark plan?
[27:22] Priya Nair: Yes, we'll propose a plan: 1) run your prompts on current OpenAI setup, capture outputs and latencies; 2) run same prompts on Redwood Dedicated with matching model and tokenization; 3) run with quantized profiles (int8/int4) to measure cost/quality tradeoffs; 4) load test for concurrency. We'll provide scripts and a spreadsheet to compare.

[31:55] Maya Torres: Network-wise, we need VPC peering and private egress; can Redwood Dedicated be deployed in our cloud project or do you host the infra?
[32:05] Jordan Lee: We offer both: Dedicated hosted in our cloud with VPC peering, or Private deployment where the control plane is customer-managed and we ship an on-prem package. For strict data residency you can host in your VPC or run our private deployment.

[35:40] Evan Chen: Pricing — what are typical commit sizes? we want a TCO calc comparing current OpenAI spend vs Redwood Dedicated.
[35:48] Jordan Lee: We'll send a Dedicated sizing worksheet — typical customers commit monthly or annual GPU capacity; pricing depends on instance types and whether you want burst. We'll include an L4/L5 breakdown and example TCO for your current token volume.

[39:10] Sanjay Patel: Any caveats re: model changes / rollouts? If we pin a model version, how do you handle security patches or bug fixes?
[39:22] Priya Nair: You can pin versions; we support canary rollouts and emergency security patches can be applied with notified maintenance windows. We also keep compatibility matrices.

[42:05] Evan Chen: For the eval parity, some of our prompts are very sensitive to small wording changes. Is there a way to run A/B tests during rollout?
[42:15] Jordan Lee: Absolutely — Redwood supports A/B and canary rollouts, and you can route a percent of traffic to a variant. We can instrument evaluation hooks and provide per-route metrics to monitor regressions.

[45:30] Maya Torres: Operationally, what does failover look like if Dedicated has an outage — automatic fallback to hosted?
[45:40] Jordan Lee: We offer smart routing: policy-based fallback to hosted API or alternative region. For Dedicated customers you can enable automatic fallback to a lower tier, with guardrails to protect secrets/data as needed.

[48:55] Evan Chen: Next steps for us: we'll share the prompt set subset and token metrics, you send pricing and benchmark plan, and then schedule the parity run.
[49:08] Jordan Lee: Great, i'll follow up with pricing and the sizing worksheet and Priya will put together the benchmark plan. We'll target the week of 2025-04-21 for the parity run.
[50:02] Maya Torres: Thanks, also please include SOC2 and network diagrams in the follow up.
[50:10] Jordan Lee: Will do. Thanks everyone.

CLOSING NOTES:
- Artifacts referenced: Redwood Dedicated deck (link sent post-call), SOC2 report, Dedicated sizing worksheet, benchmark plan/spreadsheet.
- Meeting ended: 2025-04-09T16:52:00Z
